mermaid:
flowchart TD
 A([Form received in registrar shared inbox]) --> B["Log in Late Add/Drop tracker (student ID, course, add or drop, date received)"]
 B --> C{Instructor signature present?}
 C -->|No| D[Email student to get form signed and resubmit]
 D --> E{Signed form returned within 10 business days?}
 E -->|No| F["Mark tracker 'Closed - incomplete'"]
 F --> Z([End])
 E -->|Yes| G{Add or drop?}
 C -->|Yes| G
 G -->|Drop| K[Enter change in SIS]
 G -->|Add| H[Check seat availability in SIS]
 H --> I{Seat available?}
 I -->|Yes| K
 I -->|No| J[Forward form to department coordinator for capacity override]
 J --> J2{Coordinator approves override?}
 J2 -->|Yes| K
 J2 -->|No| J3[Notify student that override was not approved]
 J3 --> Z
 K --> L["Email student 'Late Change Confirmed' template and cc instructor"]
 L --> M["Mark tracker row 'Complete'"]
 M --> Z
summary: This process handles paper/PDF late add/drop forms from students who missed the online deadline. Each form is logged in the tracker and checked for the instructor's signature; if it is missing, the student is asked to resubmit, and the item is closed as incomplete after 10 business days without a response. Signed drops are entered in the SIS directly, while adds require a seat check, and full sections need the department coordinator's capacity override first. Once entered, the student is emailed a confirmation with the instructor cc'd and the tracker row is marked Complete. Note that the notes do not say what happens if the coordinator denies the override, so that branch (notify the student) is an assumption to confirm.

mermaid:
flowchart TD
 A([Password reset request received]) --> B["Log ticket: Access > Password Reset"]
 B --> C["Verify caller: employee ID + security question answer"]
 C --> D{Verification passed?}
 D -->|Yes| E{"Account expired or locked?"}
 D -->|No| F["Do not reset; tell caller to come to desk in person with badge"]
 F --> G["Put ticket on hold and note 'ID not verified'"]
 G --> H{"Wrong 3 times in one call?"}
 H -->|Yes| I["Flag account to Security"]
 I --> J([Our part is closed])
 H -->|No| K([Ticket on hold awaiting in-person visit])
 E -->|Expired| L["Send self-service reset link to registered mobile"]
 E -->|Locked| M["Unlock account in admin console"]
 M --> L
 L --> N["Stay on line or chat until caller confirms login works"]
 N --> O["Close ticket with one-line note of action taken"]
 O --> P([Done])
summary: Every password reset request is logged first as an Access > Password Reset ticket, and then the caller is verified with their employee ID and security question answer. If verification fails, no reset is done; the caller is told to visit the desk in person with their badge and the ticket is put on hold with the note "ID not verified", and if they failed 3 times in one call the account is also flagged to Security, which closes the help desk's part. If verification passes, the agent checks whether the account is expired or locked: expired accounts get a self-service reset link sent to their registered mobile, while locked accounts are unlocked in the admin console first and then sent the same link. The agent stays with the caller until they confirm they can log in, then closes the ticket with a short summary of what was done.
